_what: Every narration sentence maps to a span of script/essay.txt, the assembled sources of record for this film.
thesis: Three valuations of one ordinary object disagree; Chang took the disagreement as the material, destroyed the coins into a block and inscribed them, and the value of what remains goes on being redefined after the coin itself has stopped being made.
epoch_convention: The film speaks from its own present (2026). A source deictic - now, currently, still, today - resolves to the SOURCE'S date and must be converted to an absolute date on the way into narration. Three moments kept distinct: THEN 2017-2024 (March 2024 project description governs), SINCE Feb-Nov 2025, NOW 2026.

claims.say: A copper cent, struck in 1972, green with verdigris, its date legible through the corrosion.
claims.span: one cent at close range, its copper face almost covered by heavy green verdigris, the 1972 date and LIBERTY legend readable through it
claims.epoch_note: Description of a rights-cleared asset, not of a claim in the written sources.

claims.say: One of ten thousand that Rutherford Chang took out of circulation, photographed, and numbered.
claims.span: CENTS is made from 10,000 American pennies minted before 1982 and valued for their copper content
claims.epoch_note: 'numbered' rests on the catalogue: 10,000 records, contiguous and without duplicates.

claims.say: To the Treasury a penny is worth one cent, whatever year it was struck, and always will be.
claims.span: a penny from any given year will always be worth exactly 1¢, according to the United States Treasury
claims.epoch_note: The span supports 'always'.

claims.say: Those struck before 1983 are copper, and in March 2024 that copper was worth about three cents.
claims.span: those minted in 1982 and before were struck in copper and now have a metal value of approximately 3.1¢
claims.epoch_note: THE MODEL CASE. The source's 'now' is March 2024 and is converted to an absolute date.

claims.say: In fiscal 2024 the Mint reported that making one cost nearly four.
claims.span: The US Mint reported that each penny cost nearly four cents to produce in fiscal 2024
claims.epoch_note: The fourth valuation, and the one no earlier cut used.

claims.say: And for more than a century it has circulated, considered a worthless nuisance.
claims.span: the lowly denomination has become so commonplace that it is considered a worthless nuisance
claims.epoch_note: Production ended November 2025; the coins remain legal tender and circulate, so the present perfect is accurate.

claims.say: Four valuations of one small object, and no two of them agree.
claims.span: Recognizing these discrepancies in value
claims.epoch: standing claim; the figures it rests on are dated in the four preceding lines
claims.epoch_note: COUNTED: four figures are named in the four preceding sentences - 1 cent, about 3 cents, nearly 4 cents, worthless.

claims.say: Chang spent twenty years collecting ordinary things until time made them singular.
claims.span: in line with the late artist's lifelong practice of obsessive collecting
claims.epoch_note: Twenty years from the exhibition record, 2002-2024.

claims.say: Three and a half thousand copies of one Beatles record, no two worn alike.
claims.span: The materials list for the UCCA retrospective (2026) gives 3,555 records and a neon sign — the later and current figure
claims.epoch_note: Two figures exist; this uses the later one. The NYT obituary (Feb 2025) gives more than 3,400.

claims.say: Shown for two decades — the New Museum in New York, the Akademie der Künste in Berlin, Kunsthal Rotterdam.
claims.span: Akademie der Kuenste, Berlin, 2021; Kunsthal Rotterdam, 2020; Deichtorhallen, Hamburg, 2019; Rhizome and the New Museum, New York, 2016
claims.epoch_note: Three institutions from the same record. The UCCA retrospective is deliberately not here: it ran after his death.

claims.say: Recognising those discrepancies in value, he removed ten thousand copper cents from circulation and called the work CENTS.
claims.span: Recognizing these discrepancies in value, Rutherford Chang removed 10,000 copper cents from circulation
claims.epoch_note: States the motive BEFORE the Brenner property that follows, so the order cannot invent one.

claims.say: Every one of the ten thousand was photographed first, one at a time, on a copy stand.
claims.span: Each coin was photographed one at a time, on a copy stand
claims.epoch_note: THE ACT. 'photographed first' is sequential, not a superlative.

claims.say: The portrait on them is Victor David Brenner's Lincoln — by the project's count the most reproduced artwork on Earth, carried on 288 billion cents in existence in 2024.
claims.span: the portrait of Abraham Lincoln on the cent's obverse is the most reproduced piece of art on Earth
claims.epoch: standing claim in the source; not independently verified
claims.epoch_note: A superlative about a set nobody can count. Attributed in narration to the project's count and dated. Flagged for the author.

claims.say: Circulation made the marks.
claims.span: The course of history has endowed each of these metal discs with unique characteristics
claims.epoch_note: Circulation made the marks. The NAMES are a separate claim four sentences later.

claims.say: Verdigris and obsidian and desert.
claims.span: Patina: verdigris, obsidian, desert, red, gold, orange, corroded, iridescent
claims.epoch_note: Trait names, spoken. Patina family.

claims.say: Abraded, faceless, striated.
claims.span: Wear: abraded, faceless, lustrous, striated
claims.epoch_note: Wear family.

claims.say: A fingerprint.
claims.span: Motif: assassin, fingerprint, ghost, wheat
claims.epoch_note: Motif family - fingerprint.

claims.say: A ghost.
claims.span: Motif: assassin, fingerprint, ghost, wheat
claims.epoch_note: Motif family - ghost.

claims.say: Wheat.
claims.span: Motif: assassin, fingerprint, ghost, wheat
claims.epoch_note: Motif family - wheat.

claims.say: Nineteen traits in five families, and no algorithm assigned any of them.
claims.span: The trait codebook holds 19 traits in five families
claims.epoch_note: 'No algorithm assigned any of them' holds the marks apart from the naming.

claims.say: The names came afterwards, from the collectors, over two years of voting on the full set.
claims.span: a community-led initiative carried out over the course of 2 years through multiple reviews of the full 10k set, numerous voting rounds
claims.epoch_note: The naming was human and came after the marks.

claims.say: Five thousand three hundred and six carry no mark at all — more than half — which is what makes the rest mean anything.
claims.span: 5,306 cents — 53.06 per cent — carry no catalogued visual trait at all
claims.epoch_note: A measurement of a closed set, so it does not expire.

claims.say: Then he destroyed them, smelted into one block of thirty-one kilograms.
claims.span: the physical coins are smelted and cast into a solid 68.56-pound copper block
claims.epoch_note: 68.56 pounds is 31 kilograms.

claims.say: Each photograph he inscribed on a satoshi, the smallest unit of Bitcoin.
claims.span: Images of these 10,000 individuals are inscribed as ordinals on 10,000 satoshis, the smallest units of Bitcoin
claims.epoch_note: TEN THOUSAND SATOSHIS, one per image - not the block. The distinction the last film's imagery collapsed.

claims.say: Ten thousand images, ten thousand satoshis.
claims.span: Images of these 10,000 individuals are inscribed as ordinals on 10,000 satoshis, the smallest units of Bitcoin
claims.epoch_note: Restates the one-to-one mapping so no shot can imply the block was the thing inscribed.

claims.say: The block itself he had scanned, and inscribed the model as the whole of Bitcoin block 839969.
claims.span: He then inscribed a 3D model of the block on a block of the blockchain (what is known as a full-block inscription)
claims.epoch_note: The MODEL of the block, inscribed as a whole block. A separate act from the 10,000.

claims.say: Where a block ordinarily carries thousands of transactions, that one carries a single object.
claims.span: Where a block ordinarily carries thousands of transactions, that one carries a single object
claims.epoch_note: Explains the full-block inscription rather than asserting a block number.

claims.say: He released all ten thousand at one satoshi each, into permissionless exchange and continual revaluation.
claims.span: he released the 10,000 cent inscriptions for the price of one sat each (apx. $ 0.0001), placing them into a system of permissionless exchange and indeterminate, continual revaluation
claims.epoch_note: The release, and the source's own language for the thesis.

claims.say: Chang died in February 2025, at forty-five, on the day the President ordered the Treasury to stop making pennies.
claims.span: On the ninth of February 2025 the President of the United States ordered the Treasury to stop making pennies
claims.as_of: NYT obituary 9 Feb 2025; penny facts of record
claims.epoch_note: Same-day: the order was announced the evening of 9 February 2025.

claims.say: The last was struck that November.
claims.span: The United States Mint struck the last cent in November 2025 and permanently suspended penny production
claims.epoch_note: The hinge, not the ending: four more sentences follow it.

claims.say: The set is closed.
claims.span: The collection holds 10,000 records exactly, contiguous and without duplicates
claims.epoch_note: Closed because no later cent is copper.

claims.say: It stops at 1982, because in 1983 the penny stopped being copper.
claims.span: Cents minted in 1982 and earlier were struck in copper; from 1983 the cent was made of zinc
claims.epoch_note: Historical and fixed.

claims.say: Eight hundred and sixty-seven of them are dated 1982, and none later.
claims.span: 867 cents are dated 1982 and none later
claims.epoch_note: Concretises the edge the next sentences argue about.

claims.say: Fifteen years are missing from it, and only one of those absences means anything: in 1943 the copper went to the war, and the cent was struck in steel.
claims.span: Fifteen years between 1910 and 1982 are absent from the collection. Only the absence of 1943 is anomalous
claims.epoch_note: THE COUNTED CLAIM. Established by counting the set, not from one member. P(zero by chance) 2.75e-05.

claims.say: A set with edges nobody chose.
claims.span: Cents minted in 1982 and earlier were struck in copper; from 1983 the cent was made of zinc
claims.epoch_note: Follows from the material change, not from a choice.

claims.say: Philip Tinari, who directs UCCA in Beijing, had written on the work for Taschen's On NFTs.
claims.span: PHILIP TINARI on CENTS — in On NFTs, ed. Robert Alice, Taschen
claims.epoch_note: Critical standing, placed with the retrospective rather than in the biography.

claims.say: In 2026, a year after his death, UCCA gave Chang his first institutional retrospective, co-curated by Tinari, Aki Sasamoto and Danielle Chang.
claims.span: CENTS was exhibited in Hundreds and Thousands at UCCA Beijing, the first institutional and most comprehensive solo exhibition of Rutherford Chang's work
claims.epoch_note: POSTHUMOUS, and placed after the death deliberately: the work goes on being shown. Three curators per the live page.

claims.say: CENTS was in it — the ten thousand on touchscreens, and the block among the materials.
claims.span: At UCCA the collection could be explored on touchscreens or in a book, decades of circulation legible in the abrasions and discolouration of individual coins
claims.epoch_note: CENTS Block 839969 appears in the exhibition materials list.

claims.say: Released at one satoshi.
claims.span: he released the 10,000 cent inscriptions for the price of one sat each
claims.epoch_note: Restated to set the comparison the next sentence makes.

claims.say: By October 2026 a hundred and ninety-eight of them were listed for sale, asking around three hundred and sixty thousand satoshis each.
claims.span: the listed asking prices observed in October 2026 are around three hundred and sixty thousand satoshis each
claims.epoch_note: NOW. 198 open listings, ASKING prices, not sales and not a valuation of the whole set.

claims.say: The cent from 1972 no longer exists.
claims.span: the physical coins are smelted and cast into a solid 68.56-pound copper block
claims.epoch_note: The object was destroyed. What persists is the inscription.

claims.say: Its image does, and what that is worth goes on being decided.
claims.span: placing them into a system of permissionless exchange and indeterminate, continual revaluation
claims.epoch_note: Closes on the image and on the value still moving, not on an ending.

distinctions_kept.distinction: a PROPERTY of the readymade (the Lincoln portrait's ubiquity) vs the artist's MOTIVE

distinctions_kept.note: Caught twice by the user. The first film opened on Brenner; so did the first draft of this one. The source itself puts the ubiquity in its second paragraph, after the discrepancies.

distinctions_kept.where: lines 13-15 say circulation made the marks and the names came afterwards, from the collectors, over two years of voting

the end of the PENNY vs the end of CENTS
distinctions_kept.where: line 27 ends the coin; line 28 continues the work. The film's last movement is in the present continuous.

distinctions_kept.distinction: CENTS Block Copper (the physical block) vs CENTS Block 839969 (the inscription of its model)
distinctions_kept.where: line 17 smelts the physical block; line 19 inscribes the scan of it

distinctions_kept.distinction: a melt value NOW vs a melt value WHEN THE WORK WAS MADE
